summary: A licensed clinician (LPC, LCSW, LMFT or psychologist) or allied wellness practitioner who treats problematic technology use, from ICD-11 gaming disorder (6C51) to compulsive social media and smartphone use, in private practice, residential programs like reSTART, schools, and employer wellbeing schemes. AI helps most with evidence synthesis, structured treatment and relapse-prevention planning, de-identified documentation, psychoeducation materials, and keeping up with fast-moving youth online-safety policy, while the therapist keeps every diagnostic and clinical judgment.

prompts.title: Intake assessment plan
prompts.task: Choose validated screening tools and structure a first session for a new client
prompts.prompt: You are assisting a licensed [LICENSE TYPE] therapist preparing an intake for a [AGE]-year-old client referred for [PRESENTING CONCERN, e.g. 6+ hours daily gaming, failing classes]. Recommend a short battery of validated screening instruments (e.g. IGDS9-SF, Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale, Smartphone Addiction Scale-Short Version, Internet Addiction Test) suitable for this age and concern, noting each tool's cut-offs, validation populations and known limitations. Then draft a 60-minute intake outline covering usage history, function of use, sleep, mood, co-occurring ADHD/anxiety/depression screening, family context and safety risk. Output: a table of instruments, then a timed session outline. Flag where ICD-11 6C51 and DSM-5-TR Section III criteria differ, and note that screening scores are not diagnoses.
prompts.caution: Screening tools support but never replace clinical diagnosis; check licensing and copyright terms for each instrument.

prompts.title: Individualized treatment plan
prompts.task: Draft a measurable treatment plan from de-identified case notes
prompts.prompt: Act as a clinical writing assistant for a therapist treating problematic technology use. From these de-identified notes: [PASTE NOTES WITHOUT NAMES, DOB, SCHOOL OR EMPLOYER], draft a treatment plan using an evidence-informed approach such as CBT-IA, motivational interviewing and family-based work where relevant. Include: problem statements, 3-4 SMART goals framed as healthy-use targets rather than total abstinence unless clinically indicated, interventions per goal, measures for tracking progress (e.g. repeat screening scores, sleep logs, screen-time reports), and a review date. Output as a standard treatment plan in [FORMAT: e.g. SOAP-compatible / agency template]. Highlight any assumptions you made and areas where the evidence base for digital-use interventions is thin.
prompts.caution: Never paste identifiable client information into a non-HIPAA-compliant tool; the clinician finalizes and owns the plan.

prompts.title: Usage data interpretation
prompts.task: Turn a client's screen-time export into patterns to discuss in session
prompts.prompt: I'm a therapist reviewing screen-time data a client consented to share, exported from [SOURCE: iOS Screen Time / Android Digital Wellbeing / RescueTime]. Data (de-identified): [PASTE DAILY OR WEEKLY TOTALS, PICKUPS, NOTIFICATIONS, TOP APPS, TIME-OF-DAY]. Identify patterns relevant to treatment: late-night use and likely sleep displacement, high-pickup windows, app categories driving use, weekday vs weekend differences, and change since [BASELINE DATE]. Output: 5-7 bullet observations, each with a non-judgmental question I could ask the client to explore its function, plus a note on the data's limitations (e.g. multiple devices, passive vs active use not distinguished, self-tracking reactivity).
prompts.caution: Device metrics are proxies; avoid treating raw hours as a measure of harm without clinical context.

prompts.title: Family media agreement
prompts.task: Co-create a family technology plan for a teen client and parents
prompts.prompt: Help me, a family therapist, draft a family media agreement for a household with [CHILDREN'S AGES] and these concerns: [CONCERNS, e.g. phone in bed, conflict over gaming time, parent's own scrolling]. Base it on reputable guidance such as the AAP Family Media Plan and the 2023 US Surgeon General advisory on social media and youth mental health. Include: tech-free zones and times, bedtime device parking, how exceptions are negotiated, parents' reciprocal commitments, a graduated autonomy path tied to the teen's age, and a monthly review ritual. Write it in plain, collaborative language at a [READING LEVEL] level, as a one-page document with signature lines, followed by tips for me on facilitating the conversation without it becoming punitive.
prompts.caution: Avoid covert monitoring recommendations that could damage trust or raise privacy concerns for older teens.

prompts.title: Relapse prevention plan
prompts.task: Build a personalized lapse/relapse plan before discharge or step-down
prompts.prompt: You are supporting a therapist preparing a client to step down from [LEVEL OF CARE, e.g. a residential program / weekly outpatient] after treatment for [CONDITION, e.g. gaming disorder]. Using these de-identified details: [TRIGGERS, HIGH-RISK SITUATIONS, COPING SKILLS THAT WORKED, SUPPORTS, UPCOMING TRANSITIONS like college or new job], draft a relapse prevention plan in the style of Marlatt's model. Include: early warning signs, an if-then plan for each top trigger, environmental controls (app limits, device placement, blocking tools like Freedom or built-in OS settings), a lapse-vs-relapse response script that avoids abstinence-violation shame, and when to contact the clinician. Output as a client-facing one-pager plus a brief clinician note on follow-up cadence.
prompts.caution: Include crisis resources (e.g. 988 in the US) if there is any history of self-harm; clinician reviews before sharing.

prompts.title: School or workplace workshop
prompts.task: Design a psychoeducation session for a group audience
prompts.prompt: Design a [LENGTH]-minute psychoeducation workshop on healthy technology use for [AUDIENCE: e.g. grade 8 students / parents / remote employees at a tech firm]. Goals: [GOALS]. Draw on reputable evidence (attention and notification research, sleep and screens, persuasive design features like infinite scroll and variable rewards) and accurately represent where findings are contested, e.g. the debate over causal links between social media and adolescent depression. Output: learning objectives, a timed agenda, 2 interactive activities, 6-8 slide headlines with speaker notes, and a short take-home handout. Avoid fear-based messaging and moral panic; emphasize agency and specific habits. List the key sources I should verify before presenting.
prompts.caution: Verify every cited study yourself; the research on screen time and wellbeing is mixed and evolving.

prompts.title: Policy and regulation briefing
prompts.task: Stay current on laws affecting youth technology use and clinical practice
prompts.prompt: I'm a therapist specializing in problematic technology use, practicing in [JURISDICTION]. Brief me on laws and policies that affect my clients and practice, such as youth social media age limits (e.g. Australia's under-16 restriction), the UK Online Safety Act, the EU Digital Services Act protections for minors, US state laws on minors' social media and school phone bans, and the status of proposals like the Kids Online Safety Act. For each: what it requires, current status as of your knowledge cutoff, and practical implications for families I counsel. Output a table plus 3 talking points for parents. Clearly mark anything that may have changed, been enjoined in court, or that you are unsure of.
prompts.caution: Laws in this area change fast and face litigation; confirm current status from official sources before advising clients.

prompts.title: Ethics and boundaries check
prompts.task: Reason through a tricky ethical or scope-of-practice situation
prompts.prompt: Act as a consultation partner for a [LICENSE TYPE] therapist in [JURISDICTION]. Situation: [DESCRIBE, e.g. a parent asks me to review their 16-year-old's private messages; an employer wants aggregate 'detox compliance' reports from a wellness program; a client wants to do sessions only by text]. Walk through the relevant principles from [CODE: e.g. ACA Code of Ethics / NASW Code / APA Ethics Code], confidentiality and minor-consent rules, HIPAA considerations for any digital tools involved, and telehealth standards. Output: the key ethical tensions, 2-3 options with pros and cons, questions I should take to supervision or my licensing board, and documentation I should keep. Do not give a definitive legal answer; flag where I need a lawyer or board guidance.
prompts.caution: This supports, not replaces, clinical supervision, legal counsel, and licensing-board guidance.
